title_en: Shenzhen Qidi Information Technology Co., Ltd. v. Zhengzhou Guohua Investment Co., Ltd., Kaifeng Yuxin Enterprise Management Consulting Co., Ltd., and Zhuhai Kemei Education Investment Co., Ltd. — dispute over equity confirmation
ruling_gist_en: Where the registered capital of a company meets the statutory requirements, the actual capital contributions and the proportion of equity held by each shareholder shall fall within the scope of shareholder autonomy. The proportion of equity held by a shareholder is generally consistent with the proportion of their actual capital contribution. However, all shareholders of a limited liability company may internally agree to hold equity not in proportion to their actual capital contributions. Such an agreement does not affect the realization of the company's basic external functions, such as providing capital as security for the company's debts. If the agreement reflects the true intention of all parties, does not harm the interests of others, and does not violate laws or administrative regulations, it shall be valid, and the equity held by shareholders in accordance with the agreement shall be protected by law.

full_text_en:
Shenzhen Qidi Information Technology Co., Ltd. v.
Zhengzhou Guohua Investment Co., Ltd., Kaifeng Yuxin Enterprise
Management Consulting Co., Ltd., and Zhuhai Kemei Education Investment
Co., Ltd. — dispute over equity confirmation

[Ruling Summary]

Where the registered capital of a company meets the statutory requirements, the actual amount of capital contributions made by each shareholder and the proportion of shares held shall fall within the scope of the autonomy of the company's shareholders. The proportion of shares held by a shareholder is generally consistent with the proportion of his actual capital contribution. However, all shareholders of a limited liability company may also internally agree not to hold shares in proportion to the actual capital contributions. Such an agreement does not affect the realization of the company's basic external functions, such as the guarantee of corporate capital for corporate claims. If the agreement represents the true intent of the parties concerned, does not harm the interests of others, and does not violate the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, it shall be valid, and the shares held by shareholders in accordance with the agreement shall be protected by law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 6

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shenzhen Qidi Information Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 407, Teaching Building, Shenzhen Youth College, Futian District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Cao Biqiong, Chairwoman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Liu Jijun, Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Wei Guotao, Lawyer of Zhongfang Law Firm, Beijing.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Zhengzhou Guohua Investment Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 2803, Building 9, No. 116 Jiankang Road, Jinshui District, Zhengzhou City, Henan Province.
Legal Representative: Zhang Jun, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Duan Keqiang, Lawyer of Shangyuan Law Firm, Beijing.
Agent ad litem: Liu Haiwei, Lawyer of Henan Golden Sunshine Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Kaifeng Yuxin Enterprise Management Consulting Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 71 Yingbin Road, Kaifeng City, Henan Province.
Legal Representative: Lian Qisheng, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Weijie, Lawyer of Henan Qingyang Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Zhuhai Kemei Education Investment Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 2 (II), Area B, 20th Floor East, Gongshang Building, No. 125 Renmin East Road, Xiangzhou, Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Zhang Jun, Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Agent ad litem: Duan Xianshi, Lawyer of Henan Jiandi Law Firm.

In the case of equity confirmation dispute between the applicant for retrial, Shenzhen Qidi Information Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qidi Company), and the respondent, Zhengzhou Guohua Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guohua Company), the defendant at first instance, Kaifeng Yuxin Enterprise Management Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuxin Company), and the third party at first instance, Zhuhai Kemei Education Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kemei Investment Company), Qidi Company, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2009) Yu Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 20 rendered by the Henan High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered a civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 866 on September 26, 2010, deciding to bring the case for retrial, and lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Wang Dongmin as presiding judge, and acting judges Liu Chongli and Zeng Hongwei as members, with Bai Xue serving as court clerk. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

On July 18, 2007, Guohua Company filed a lawsuit with the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province, alleging: On October 26, 2006, Guohua Company, Qidi Company, and Yuxin Company signed the "Investment Agreement on the Formation of Zhuhai Kemei Education Investment Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "October 26 Agreement"), agreeing to form Kemei Investment Company, and stipulating the capital contributions, shareholding ratios, and other matters among the three parties. After the "October 26 Agreement" was signed, Guohua Company fulfilled its capital contribution obligations, while Qidi Company and Yuxin Company failed to make capital contributions but abused their shareholder rights, thereby harming Guohua Company's rights and interests. Therefore, Guohua Company requested a judgment: 1. That all equity in Kemei Investment Company be vested in Guohua Company. 2. If the first request of Guohua Company could not be granted, to rule according to law that Kemei Investment Company be dissolved and liquidated. Yuxin Company raised a jurisdictional objection. After trial, the court of first instance rejected Yuxin Company's objection; Yuxin Company appealed, and the court of second instance upheld the ruling of first instance rejecting the objection. Qidi Company argued in defense: Guohua Company, after thorough investigation, decided to cooperate with Qidi Company. The expression of intent by the three parties that the capital contributions of Qidi Company and Yuxin Company would be paid by Guohua Company was genuine and complied with the provisions of the Company Law. The 55% equity held by Qidi Company in Kemei Investment Company was lawful. Guohua Company's request to dissolve the company also lacked factual and legal basis. Guohua Company's claims should be dismissed. Yuxin Company's defense arguments were the same as those of Qidi Company.

The Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court found after trial at first instance: On September 18, 2006, with Liu Jijun as Party A and Zhang Jun as Party B, they signed the "Agreement on Cooperative Construction of the Engineering Technology College of Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai Campus" (hereinafter referred to as the "September 18 Agreement"), stipulating that the two parties would jointly establish Zhuhai Kemei Education Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kemei Consulting Company), and in the name of the company, sign a cooperation agreement with Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai Campus (hereinafter referred to as Zhuhai Campus), to jointly build and operate the Engineering Technology College of Zhuhai Campus (hereinafter referred to as the Engineering College of Zhuhai Campus). Party A, with educational capital (including educational theories and concepts, integration and introduction of educational resources, educational operation and management teams, and planning and implementation of educational projects), would hold 70% of the shares of Kemei Consulting Company. Party B, with a capital investment of RMB 70 million in the construction and operation of the Engineering College of Zhuhai Campus, would hold 30% of the shares of Kemei Consulting Company. Within 10 days after the signing of this agreement, Party B would deposit RMB 5 million as a performance bond into the account of Kemei Consulting Company, and this agreement would take effect. Before Kemei Consulting Company signed the agreement with Zhuhai Campus, the bond could not be used. Within 15 days after the signing of the agreement between Kemei Consulting Company and Zhuhai Campus, Party B would transfer RMB 15 million into a joint escrow account of Kemei Consulting Company and Zhuhai Campus, and at the same time, Party B would transfer the RMB 5 million bond already deposited in Kemei Consulting Company to Zhuhai Campus as a performance bond. Within 90 days after Kemei Consulting Company signed the agreement with Zhuhai Campus, Party B would transfer RMB 10 million into the escrow account, and the remaining RMB 40 million would be transferred into the escrow account in line with the progress of the project. Before Party B's investment of RMB 70 million was fully recovered, the distribution ratio between the parties in Kemei Consulting Company would be 20% to 80%. After the RMB 70 million was fully recovered, the distribution would be in proportion to the shareholding ratio. On September 30, 2006, Guohua Company deposited RMB 5 million as a bond into the account of Kemei Consulting Company (Bank: Agricultural Bank of China, Jinding Sub-branch, Account No.: 44353401040003686). On October 24, 2006, the RMB 5 million bond was transferred from the account of Kemei Consulting Company to the account of Qidi Company. On October 26, 2006, Guohua Company, Qidi Company, and Yuxin Company signed the "October 26 Agreement" stipulating: (1) Guohua Company would contribute RMB 3 million in cash, accounting for 30% of the company's registered capital; Yuxin Company would contribute RMB 1.5 million in cash, accounting for 15% of the registered capital; Qidi Company would contribute RMB 5.5 million in cash, accounting for 55% of the registered capital. The three parties agreed to promptly deposit the capital contributions into the preparatory committee account of the newly established company. (2) Provisions were made regarding the operation and profit distribution of the proposed cooperative school-running project with Zhuhai Campus. (3) It was agreed that Qidi Company would handle the industrial and commercial registration procedures for Kemei Investment Company. (4) Zhang Jun, representing Guohua Company, would serve as the Chairman of the Board and legal representative of Kemei Investment Company. (5) The total registered capital of RMB 10 million and the total investment of RMB 60 million for the company would all be raised and contributed by Guohua Company. On the same day, the "Articles of Association of Zhuhai Kemei Education Investment Co., Ltd." was adopted, stipulating: The registered capital of the company is RMB 10 million. Qidi Company subscribed for RMB 5.5 million, representing 55%; Guohua Company subscribed for RMB 3 million, representing 30%; Yuxin Company subscribed for RMB 1.5 million, representing 15%. Each shareholder shall pay in full the amount of capital they have subscribed before the company's registration. The Chairman of the Board shall be appointed by Guohua Company, and the Vice Chairman by Qidi Company. In case of conflict between the Articles of Association and the "October 26 Agreement", the "October 26 Agreement" shall prevail. On October 25, 2006, at the request of Yuxin Company and Qidi Company, Guohua Company transferred RMB 1.5 million to Yuxin Company and RMB 500,000 to Qidi Company. Yuxin Company transferred the aforementioned RMB 1.5 million into the account of Kemei Consulting Company (which also served as the preparatory committee account of Kemei Investment Company) as its subscribed capital. Qidi Company transferred the RMB 500,000 received from Guohua Company and the RMB 5 million bond transferred from the account of Kemei Consulting Company on October 24 into the account of Kemei Consulting Company as its subscribed capital. Guohua Company transferred RMB 3 million into the account of Kemei Consulting Company as its subscribed capital. On October 31, 2006, with the approval of the Zhuhai Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, Kemei Consulting Company changed its name to Kemei Investment Company. The registered capital was increased from RMB 500,000 to RMB 10 million, and the shareholders changed from Lou Hongtao, Liu Jijun, and Zhao Shengyun to Guohua Company, Qidi Company, and Yuxin Company. On the same day, Kemei Investment Company and Zhuhai Campus signed the "Agreement on Cooperative Establishment of the Engineering Technology College of Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai Campus", stipulating the specific matters of the cooperative school-running project. On November 28, 2006, Liu Jijun and Zhang Jun signed a "Memorandum of Cooperation" stipulating: (1) Both parties agreed to rename Kemei Consulting Company as Kemei Investment Company. (2) The company's shareholders shall consist of legal persons, with Qidi Company and Yuxin Company representing Party A, and Guohua Company representing Party B. All registered capital shall be paid by Party B. Thereafter, Guohua Company gradually invested RMB 17.5 million, totaling RMB 27.5 million including the RMB 10 million capital contribution. Qidi Company acknowledged that Guohua Company only took over the account of Kemei Investment Company after November 2, 2006. During the cooperative school-running process between Kemei Investment Company and Zhuhai Campus, conflicts arose between the parties, and disputes also emerged as to whether to continue cooperation with Zhuhai Campus. Guohua Company then filed this lawsuit.

The Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court held at first instance that Article 27 of the Company Law provides: Shareholders may make capital contributions in currency, or in kind, intellectual property rights, land use rights, or other non-monetary property that can be valued in currency and may be transferred according to law. Non-monetary property contributed as capital shall be evaluated and appraised. According to this provision, non-monetary property must satisfy two conditions to be used as capital contribution: first, it must be capable of being valued in currency; second, it must be legally transferable. Additionally, an evaluation and appraisal process must be carried out. The provision in the "September 18 Agreement" (with Liu Jijun as Party A and Zhang Jun as Party B) that Party A would contribute educational capital, accounting for 70% of the shares of Kemei Consulting Company, clearly did not satisfy the conditions for non-monetary capital contributions under this provision, and no evaluation or appraisal was conducted. That provision is not legally binding on the parties. Comparing the "October 26 Agreement" signed by Guohua Company, Qidi Company, and Yuxin Company with the "September 18 Agreement", the following changes occurred: First, the parties were replaced by Qidi Company and Yuxin Company in place of Liu Jijun, and Guohua Company in place of Zhang Jun. However, the identities of the parties in the two agreements were highly connected with no substantive change, and all parties did not object to this. Second, Liu Jijun's 70% share was changed to Qidi Company and Yuxin Company jointly holding 70% of the shares, and Liu Jijun's capital contribution in the form of educational capital became Guohua Company's undertaking to raise and pay the capital contributions for Qidi Company and Yuxin Company. Under this arrangement, Qidi Company and Yuxin Company still had no obligation to make capital contributions, which was essentially no different from the educational capital contribution arrangement, but circumvented relevant laws and regulations. The result of Guohua Company raising and paying the capital contributions for Qidi Company and Yuxin Company was that Guohua Company, as the actual investor, held only 30% of the company's shares, while Qidi Company and Yuxin Company, which made no capital contributions, held 70% of the shares. Guohua Company, as the actual investor, sought confirmation of shares corresponding to its capital contribution, which is legally justified and consistent with equity. The "Articles of Association of the Company" signed by all shareholders of Kemei Investment Company represented the true intent of all shareholders of the company and contained no prohibited provisions. It is legally binding on the company and all shareholders. All shareholders shall pay in full the amount of capital they subscribed: Guohua Company to contribute RMB 3 million, Yuxin Company to contribute RMB 1.5 million, and Qidi Company to contribute RMB 5.5 million. Yuxin Company had transferred RMB 1.5 million into the account of Kemei Investment Company (preparatory committee) and should be deemed to have fully fulfilled its capital contribution obligation. As to whether the RMB 1.5 million was transferred by Guohua Company to Yuxin Company, that constitutes a separate legal relationship and is not addressed in this case. Guohua Company also transferred RMB 3 million into the account of Kemei Investment Company, fully fulfilling its capital contribution obligation. Based on the provision in the "September 18 Agreement" that within 10 days after the signing of the agreement, Zhang Jun should deposit RMB 5 million as a bond into the account of Kemei Consulting Company, it can be seen that Liu Jijun controlled the account of Kemei Consulting Company, while Guohua Company, chaired by Zhang Jun, only took over the account of the renamed Kemei Investment Company after November 2, 2006. Based on this, it is sufficient to conclude that the transfer of the RMB 5 million bond from the account of Kemei Consulting Company to the account of Qidi Company was made by Qidi Company. Subsequently, Qidi Company transferred the RMB 5 million back into the account of Kemei Investment Company as capital verification funds. This practice of reversing the flow of funds is contrary to good faith. The RMB 5 million shall not, according to law, be deemed as Qidi Company's capital contribution. Since the RMB 5 million was Guohua Company's investment funds and Guohua Company claims it should be recognized as its capital contribution, it shall, according to law, be recognized as Guohua Company's capital contribution. Accordingly, Guohua Company actually contributed RMB 8 million, accounting for 80% of the shares of Kemei Investment Company; Yuxin Company contributed RMB 1.5 million, accounting for 15%; and Qidi Company contributed RMB 500,000, accounting for 5%. Guohua Company's claim for a change in equity is well-founded, and the court supports it. Guohua Company's second claim, for a judgment to dissolve Kemei Investment Company and liquidate it, is an alternative claim. Since the first claim has been granted, there is no need to adjudicate the second claim. The court does not address it. Pursuant to Articles 27 and 28 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the civil judgment (2007) Bian Min Chu Zi No. 69: 1. Confirmed that Guohua Company contributed RMB 8 million, accounting for 80% of the shares of Kemei Investment Company; Yuxin Company contributed RMB 1.5 million, accounting for 15%; Qidi Company contributed RMB 500,000, accounting for 5%. 2. Dismissed the other claims of Guohua Company. The case acceptance fee of RMB 188,190 was borne by Qidi Company.

Dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, Qidi Company appealed to the Henan High People's Court, arguing: 1. According to the Articles of Association of Kemei Investment Company, Qidi Company, Yuxin Company, and Guohua Company were to contribute RMB 5.5 million, RMB 1.5 million, and RMB 3 million respectively, accounting for 55%, 15%, and 30% of the shares of Kemei Investment Company. The method of contribution was currency. On October 25, 2006, the three companies respectively transferred their contributions into the account of Kemei Investment Company, and an accounting firm issued a capital verification report. On October 31, 2006, the Zhuhai Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce approved and completed the industrial and commercial registration change. Qidi Company thereby obtained a lawful and effective shareholder status. The above procedures fully complied with the provisions of the Company Law. Qidi Company's shareholder status and the shares it held according to law were genuine, lawful, and should be protected. 2. After years of painstaking efforts, Qidi Company successfully facilitated the establishment of the Engineering College of Zhuhai Campus, and Qidi Company obtained the right to cooperate in running the school with Zhuhai Campus. Guohua Company, a professional institution with years of experience in education investment, fully understood the value of this project. Through multiple rounds of negotiations, the parties reached the "September 18 Agreement" and the "October 26 Agreement", stipulating that Guohua Company would contribute RMB 10 million to restructure Kemei Consulting Company, with the RMB 7 million contribution due from Qidi Company's 55% shares and Yuxin Company's 15% shares all to be injected by Guohua Company. Such an agreement represented the true intent of all parties, constituted a lawful commercial transaction, did not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or regulations, and should be recognized as lawful and valid. All parties performed the agreement and completed the capital contributions. Because the capital verification authority required contributions to be transferred from shareholders' accounts into the account of Kemei Investment Company, and Guohua Company did not strictly follow the capital verification authority's requirements for remittance operations, on October 26, 2006, Qidi Company returned the RMB 3 million transferred by Guohua Company into the account of Kemei Investment Company back to Guohua Company, and Guohua Company then transferred the same amount into the account of Kemei Investment Company in the name of capital contribution. Similarly, Qidi Company had to transfer the RMB 5 million from the account of Kemei Investment Company to Qidi Company's account, and then transfer it back to the account of Kemei Investment Company the next day. This method was not, as the court of first instance found, contrary to good faith, nor did it infringe upon any party's rights or interests. After Guohua Company took over the account of Kemei Investment Company, it never raised any objection to this. On November 28, 2006, the "Memorandum of Cooperation" signed by Liu Jijun and Zhang Jun once again confirmed that Guohua Company would pay all registered capital and the shareholding ratios of each shareholder. 3. Since the court of first instance recognized that Yuxin Company's contribution of RMB 1.5 million and RMB 500,000 of Qidi Company's contribution fulfilled the capital contribution obligation, it effectively acknowledged that the agreement for Guohua Company to make capital contributions on behalf of Qidi Company and Yuxin Company was lawful and valid. Yet the court of first instance refused to recognize the RMB 5 million portion of Qidi Company's contribution, resulting in obvious contradictions and logical errors. 4. Qidi Company fully performed its obligations as a shareholder. At first instance, Qidi Company submitted substantial evidence to the court demonstrating that in the cooperation between Kemei Investment Company and Zhuhai Campus, Qidi Company actively fulfilled its shareholder obligations and contractual duties. In summary, the judgment of first instance contained obvious contradictions and errors in both fact-finding and application of law, and Qidi Company requested that the court of second instance ascertain the facts and amend the judgment according to law.

Guohua Company argued: 1. The facts found by the first-instance trial were clear and the applicable law was correct. Qidi Company did not subscribe to the increased registered capital of RMB 5.5 million in monetary form as agreed and in accordance with the company's articles of association. It only deposited RMB 500,000 into the capital verification account of Kemei Investment Company. The other RMB 5 million was obtained by Qidi Company taking advantage of its control over Kemei Consulting Company's account to transfer, without authorization, the RMB 5 million deposit that Guohua Company had paid into Kemei Consulting Company's account to its own account, and then, on the following day, transferring it to the capital verification account of Kemei Investment Company as Qidi Company's capital contribution to Kemei Investment Company. Qidi Company's conduct clearly violated the principle of good faith and the principle of capital authenticity of a company. The first-instance judgment's finding that the RMB 5 million could not be considered Qidi Company's capital contribution was factually clear and legally correct. 2. The "September 18 Agreement" and the "October 26 Agreement" of 2006, which stipulated that the registered capital of RMB 10 million for the change of registration of Kemei Consulting Company was to be raised by Guohua Company, circumvented the mandatory provisions of the company laws and regulations regarding the forms of capital contribution, and were therefore invalid. Qidi Company's argument that, under these invalid agreements, it could enjoy equity in Kemei Investment Company without making an actual capital contribution could not be sustained. It requested that the original judgment be affirmed. Yuxin Company argued: It had no objection to the first-instance findings regarding Yuxin Company. Guohua Company's capital contribution on its behalf was voluntary, and the form of contribution was monetary. It requested that the rights of Qidi Company be determined according to law.

The Henan High People's Court confirmed the facts found by the first-instance trial.

The Henan High People's Court, in its second-instance trial, held: The focal issue of the dispute between Qidi Company and Guohua Company was whether the provisions in the "September 18 Agreement" and the "October 26 Agreement" signed between them, which stipulated that the registered capital of RMB 10 million for the change of registration of Kemei Consulting Company was to be raised by Guohua Company, were valid, and whether Qidi Company, which had not made an actual capital contribution under these provisions, was entitled to the equity in Kemei Investment Company. The validity of the above agreements determined whether the equity held by each party was lawful. The "September 18 Agreement" was signed by Liu Jijun, representing the project planning and operation party of the Engineering College of the Zhuhai Campus, and Zhang Jun. Liu Jijun's contribution was educational resources, while the actual contribution was made by Zhang Jun. After the signing of the "September 18 Agreement," Liu Jijun and others transferred the shareholders of Kemei Consulting Company from three individuals including Liu Jijun to Qidi Company, Guohua Company, and Yuxin Company through share transfers. On the same day, Qidi Company, Guohua Company, and Yuxin Company entered into the "October 26 Agreement" and signed the articles of association of Kemei Investment Company, stipulating the capital contributions and the corresponding equity ratios of each party. In the "October 26 Agreement," the educational resource contribution stipulated in the "September 18 Agreement" was converted into a cash contribution. The process of signing the above agreements essentially involved Liu Jijun converting his educational resources into Qidi Company's resources as a contribution, with Guohua Company being responsible for the actual cash contribution. According to relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education, ordinary institutions of higher learning primarily participate in school operation using their school name, intellectual property, management resources, education, and teaching. Social organizations or individuals primarily participate in school operation using funds, tangible assets, land use rights, etc. In this case, although Liu Jijun and others nominally made cash contributions, they were in substance making contributions with educational resources. The parties, by signing the agreements, effectively circumvented the prohibitive provisions of relevant Chinese laws. The "September 18 Agreement" should be held invalid. On the basis of this agreement, the "October 26 Agreement" reached between Qidi Company, Guohua Company, and Yuxin Company also violated the law. Guohua Company's act of making capital contributions on behalf of Qidi Company was invalid due to its violation of the law. This court confirmed the first-instance judgment's determination that Qidi Company held 5% of the equity in Kemei Investment Company and Yuxin Company held 15% of the equity in Kemei Investment Company. Qidi Company's appeal arguments that it had completed its capital contribution in accordance with the Company Law and that the "September 18 Agreement" and "October 26 Agreement" were lawful commercial transactions lacked supporting evidence and were not upheld by this court. After deliberation by the Adjudication Committee, and in accordance with Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court rendered the Civil Judgment (2009) Yu Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 20 on March 24, 2010: Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 46,800 was borne by Qidi Company.

Qidi Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment, applied to this court for retrial, alleging: (1) The original trial court's findings of the basic facts of the case and the judgment were self-contradictory and contained serious errors. The main focus of this case was whether Qidi Company's capital contribution of RMB 5 million was valid and whether its 50% equity was valid. 1. The original trial court's determination that the "September 18 Agreement" was invalid based on the relevant provisions of the "Measures for the Establishment and Management of Independent Colleges" (Order No. 26 of the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China) was erroneous. The "September 18 Agreement" was an agreement for the establishment of Kemei Consulting Company, not a cooperative school-running agreement, and the relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education should not apply. Furthermore, the "September 18 Agreement" was signed in 2006, while the Ministry of Education's Order No. 26 came into effect on April 1, 2008. The original trial court violated the principle of non-retroactivity of laws. 2. The original trial court held that the "September 18 Agreement" was invalid, the "October 26 Agreement" violated the law, and consequently held that Guohua Company's act of making capital contributions on behalf of Qidi Company was invalid, and that the 50% equity corresponding to the RMB 5 million contributed by Guohua Company on behalf of Qidi Company belonged to Guohua Company. However, it also determined that the 5% and 15% equity corresponding to the RMB 500,000 and RMB 1.5 million, also contributed by Guohua Company on behalf of the other parties, belonged to Qidi Company and Yuxin Company respectively, which was contradictory. 3. The source of Qidi Company's registered capital could not constitute the basis for determining whether its registered capital had been paid up. Qidi Company had provided the bank transfer slip, the capital verification report from the accounting firm, and the registered capital registration certificate lawfully approved by the Administration for Industry and Commerce, proving that Qidi Company's registered capital had been fully and lawfully paid in and confirmed through statutory procedures. Regardless of whether Qidi Company was entitled to use the RMB 5 million deposit, the court should not have used it as the basis for determining the ownership of the 50% equity. According to the "October 26 Agreement," the total registered capital of RMB 10 million was to be contributed entirely by Guohua Company. Guohua Company remitted RMB 1.5 million in full to Yuxin Company, but only remitted RMB 500,000 to Qidi Company. This indicated that Guohua Company not only knew about but also fully consented to Qidi Company transferring the RMB 5 million previously remitted by Guohua Company into the account of Kemei Consulting Company into Qidi Company's account to be used for the capital verification of the registered capital of the post-amendment Kemei Investment Company. This was entirely consistent with the content of the investment agreement signed by the three parties. There was no issue regarding violation of Guohua Company's true intention, nor was there the issue of "such back-and-forth flow of funds lacking good faith" as found by the first-instance trial. (2) The capital contribution status of a company's shareholders had no relationship with the equity ratio stipulated in the company's articles of association. The equity ratio, once determined by the articles of association, could not be changed without authorization. The equity ratio determined by the articles of association and confirmed by the industry and commerce authorities was binding on all shareholders and was statutory. The original trial court disregarded the true intentions of the parties and the terms of the contract and erroneously modified the shareholders' contributions and equity ratios clearly stipulated in the articles of association based on the source of funds. The "September 18 Agreement" and the "October 26 Agreement" reflected the true intentions of the parties and did not violate any national laws or regulations. Guohua Company's payment to Qidi Company and Yuxin Company for the increased registered capital of Kemei Consulting Company also did not violate any existing company law provisions. Moreover, the registered capital of Kemei Investment Company in this case was RMB 10 million entirely in monetary form. There was no issue of non-monetary contributions, and no legal provision required that the source of registered capital must be the shareholder's own funds. (3) The original trial court made an error regarding territorial jurisdiction. Disputes among company shareholders over contributions, equity allocation, etc., are accepted by the people's court in the place of the company's domicile. In this case, the company's domicile, the place of contract signing, and the place of contract performance were all in Zhuhai City. The original trial court had no jurisdiction over this case. This case should be retried by this court or transferred for retrial. In summary, it requested: 1. The revocation of the Civil Judgment (2009) Yu Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 20 of the Henan High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2007) Bian Min Chu Zi No. 69 of the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court, Henan Province; 2. Retrial by the Supreme People's Court or transfer of the case to the Zhuhai Intermediate People's Court for retrial; 3. Dismissal of all claims of the respondent in the original first-instance action; 4. The respondents to bear the litigation costs of the first instance, second instance, and the application for retrial.

The respondent, Guohua Company, argued in its defense: (1) In the process of establishing Kemei Investment Company, Qidi Company circumvented the law and did not have the legal qualifications to be a shareholder of Kemei Investment Company. On October 31, 2006, Kemei Investment Company was established. Article 7 of its articles of association provided for "monetary contributions" by Qidi Company, Yuxin Company, and Guohua Company. This clause used a lawful form to conceal an unlawful purpose, circumventing the law, and should be held invalid. Qidi Company did not have the legal qualifications to be a shareholder of Kemei Investment Company. 1. The intention behind the establishment of Kemei Investment Company indicated a motive for circumvention. Clause 1.3 of the "September 18 Agreement" signed by Liu Jijun, representing the project planning and operation party of the Engineering and Technology College of the Zhuhai Campus of Beijing Normal University, and Zhang Jun, stated: Party A contributed educational capital (including educational theories and concepts, integration and introduction of educational resources, educational operation and management team, planning and implementation of educational projects) for 70% of the shares of Kemei, and Party B contributed RMB 70 million of capital for the construction and operation of the college, accounting for 30% of the shares of Kemei. The above agreement indicated that Liu Jijun's original intention was to contribute his educational capital for 70% of the shares of Kemei Investment Company, and he had no intention to contribute RMB or other lawful non-monetary property to Kemei Investment Company. 2. Qidi Company circumvented the law during the establishment of Kemei Investment Company. (a) On October 26, 2006, Article 12 of the investment agreement signed by the three parties, titled "Operation and Investment," stated: The company's registered capital of RMB 10 million for the change of registration and the investment shortfall of RMB 60 million were to be raised and contributed entirely by Party B. Article 17 of the investment agreement stated: In case of conflict between the articles of association and this agreement, this agreement shall prevail. The above materials showed that the 70% equity held by Qidi Company and Yuxin Company in Kemei Investment Company was in substance still a contribution of educational capital. Only formally had Guohua Company replaced Zhang Jun, and Qidi Company and Yuxin Company replaced Liu Jijun. (b) Article 9 of the articles of association of Kemei Investment Company stated: Shareholders may make non-monetary contributions, but must go through relevant procedures in accordance with laws and regulations. Article 52 of the articles of association stated: In case of conflict between the contents of these articles of association and the "October 26 Agreement" of the three shareholders, the "October 26 Agreement" shall prevail. Since Qidi Company knew that non-monetary contributions were permissible, but Article 7 of the articles of association nevertheless used the "form of monetary contribution" to conceal the substance of "educational capital contribution," it was clear that Qidi Company was circumventing the law, using a lawful form to conceal an unlawful purpose. The articles of association have the highest effect on shareholders, but both the articles of association and the "October 26 Agreement" stipulated that the "October 26 Agreement" prevailed over the articles of association. Obviously, Qidi Company circumvented the law during the establishment of Kemei Investment Company. 3. The "Cooperation Memorandum" confirmed that Qidi Company circumvented the law during the establishment of Kemei Investment Company. On November 28, 2006, Liu Jijun and Zhang Jun signed the "Cooperation Memorandum," Article 1 of which stated: To meet legal requirements, the parties agreed to change the name of "Zhuhai Kemei Education Consulting Co., Ltd." to "Zhuhai Kemei Education Investment Co., Ltd.," with a registered capital of RMB 10 million. Article 2 stated: The shareholders of Kemei Investment Company shall be legal persons, among which Qidi Company (accounting for 55% of the shares of Kemei Investment Company) and Yuxin Company (accounting for 15% of the shares of Kemei Investment Company) represent Party A, and Guohua Company (accounting for 30% of the shares of Kemei Investment Company) represents Party B. The entire registered capital shall be paid by Party B and included in the total investment agreed by both parties. The above materials showed that Qidi Company did not make a capital contribution with RMB or other lawful non-monetary property, nor did it have the intention to do so. The provision of Article 7 of the articles of association of Kemei Investment Company regarding "monetary contributions by shareholders" was in substance using a lawful form to conceal an unlawful purpose, circumventing the law. (2) The contribution of educational capital violates the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations. According to Article 27(1) of the Company Law, property that laws or administrative regulations prohibit from being used as capital contribution cannot be so used. Article 14(2) of the "Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration of Companies" provides: Shareholders may not use labor services, credit, natural person names, goodwill, franchise rights, or property with security interests as capital contributions. The essence of Qidi Company's educational capital contribution was a contribution of labor services, which clearly violated the prohibitive provisions of administrative regulations. Even if educational capital were categorized as human capital, it would still not conform to the statutory forms of capital contribution. The entire registered capital of RMB 10 million of Kemei Investment Company was contributed by Guohua Company, so all the equity in Kemei Investment Company should belong to Guohua Company. In summary, Qidi Company's grounds for retrial were unsustainable, and it requested that the retrial application be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The original defendant, Yuxin Company, submitted its statement, arguing that Guohua Company was the actual capital contributor of Kemei Investment Company. Yuxin Company and Qidi Company had not actually contributed capital to Kemei Investment Company. Yuxin Company did not wish to enjoy the equity in Kemei Investment Company, nor did it wish to bear any liability for any debts of Kemei Investment Company.

The third party in the original trial, Kemei Investment Company, submitted its statement, arguing that Kemei Investment Company was in substance a single-shareholder company, with Guohua Company as its sole shareholder. The ownership of the RMB 5 million misappropriated by Qidi Company belonged to Guohua Company, so Qidi Company's capital contribution of RMB 5 million to Kemei Investment Company was invalid. It requested that the original judgment be affirmed.

In the retrial, none of the parties submitted new evidence.

This court found upon retrial: (1) Article 14 of the "October 26 Agreement" stipulated: "Profit Distribution: 1. Before the full recovery of the RMB 70 million capital contributed by Party B (i.e., Guohua Company), after the company pays income tax and withdraws statutory reserves and public welfare funds according to law, the profits shall be distributed among the three shareholders as agreed, i.e., Party A (i.e., Qidi Company) is entitled to 16% of the company's profits, Party B is entitled to 80%, and Party C (i.e., Yuxin Company) is entitled to 4%. 2. After the full recovery of the RMB 70 million capital contributed by Party B, after the company pays income tax and withdraws statutory reserves and public welfare funds according to law, the profits shall be distributed among the three shareholders in proportion to their capital contributions, i.e., Party A is entitled to 55% of the company's profits, Party B is entitled to 30%, and Party C is entitled to 15%." (2) The "September 18 Agreement" listed: Party A was the project planning and operation party of the Engineering College of the Zhuhai Campus, and Party B was Zhang Jun et al. This court confirmed the other facts found by the original trial.

In the retrial, Guohua Company explicitly stated that it was abandoning its second claim in the original trial, namely, the dissolution and liquidation of Kemei Investment Company.

This court held that the focus of the dispute between the parties was whether the equity formed by the capital contribution of RMB 5 million made in the name of Qidi Company to Kemei Investment Company should belong to Guohua Company or Qidi Company.

According to the facts found upon retrial, the "September 18 Agreement" was an agreement signed by the project planning and operation party of the Engineering College of the Zhuhai Campus as Party A, and Zhang Jun et al. as Party B, with Liu Jijun and Zhang Jun representing the respective parties, for the establishment of Kemei Consulting Company to cooperatively build the Engineering College of the Zhuhai Campus. The "October 26 Agreement" was an agreement signed by Qidi Company, Guohua Company, and Yuxin Company in their respective names regarding the formation of Kemei Investment Company. While there was indeed some connection in the motivation for signing the two agreements, the parties and the content of cooperation under the two agreements were entirely different. The two agreements were independent of each other, and there was no subordinate relationship between them. Even if the "September 18 Agreement" was invalid, it would not affect the validity of the "October 26 Agreement." The original trial's use of the validity of the "September 18 Agreement" to negate the validity of the "October 26 Agreement" was an erroneous application of law. This case was a dispute arising from Qidi Company, Guohua Company, and Yuxin Company's formation of Kemei Investment Company in fulfillment of the "October 26 Agreement." Kemei Investment Company was established by way of a change from Kemei Consulting Company: the company name changed; the shareholders changed from Lou Hongtao, Liu Jijun, and Zhao Shengyun to Guohua Company, Qidi Company, and Yuxin Company; and the registered capital of the company changed from RMB 500,000 to RMB 10 million. The "October 26 Agreement" stipulated that the RMB 10 million should be contributed in monetary form. This was the true intention of the parties and complied with Article 27 of the Company Law, which provides that shareholders may make capital contributions in monetary form. Therefore, this stipulation was valid.

The subscribed registered capital by shareholders forms the foundation of a company's capital, but effective operation of a company may sometimes require other conditions or resources. Therefore, where the registered capital meets statutory requirements, Chinese law does not prohibit shareholders from internally agreeing on their respective actual capital contributions and shareholding ratios. Such agreements do not affect the realization of the company's basic external functions such as capital serving as security for company debts, nor do they constitute circumvention of the law; rather, they fall within the scope of the autonomy of will of the company's shareholders. The "10.26 Agreement" stipulates that the entire RMB 10 million registered capital of Kemei Investment Company shall be contributed by Guohua Company, while both the agreement and the articles of association of Kemei Investment Company provide that the shareholding ratios shall be held as Qidi Company 55%, Guohua Company 35%, and Yuxin Company 15%. Article 14 of the "10.26 Agreement" provides that before Guohua Company's RMB 70 million funds are fully recovered, the company's profits shall be distributed as Qidi Company 16%, Guohua Company 80%, and Yuxin Company 4%; after Guohua Company's RMB 70 million funds are fully recovered, the company's profits shall be distributed as Qidi Company 55%, Guohua Company 30%, and Yuxin Company 15%. Based on the foregoing, Qidi Company, Guohua Company, and Yuxin Company agreed that the entire registered capital of Kemei Investment Company shall be contributed by Guohua Company, while each shareholder respectively holds the agreed share of equity in Kemei Investment Company, and also made special arrangements for distribution of the company's profits. This is the result of each party's comprehensive assessment of its own operational resources, input costs, and expected returns; it represents the true intention of each party, does not harm the interests of others, does not violate laws or administrative regulations, and constitutes a valid agreement that the parties shall perform as agreed. The said RMB 10 million has been fully contributed in accordance with the "10.26 Agreement," legally underwent capital verification, and was approved and registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce together with other changes, therefore the RMB 10 million constitutes a valid capital contribution. The RMB 5 million contribution made in the name of Qidi Company to Kemei Investment Company was initially deposited into the account of Kemei Consulting Company as a deposit, not as registered capital; it was later transferred into Qidi Company's account, and then invested into Kemei Investment Company's account to complete the capital increase. At that time, none of the shareholders raised any objection, and this RMB 5 million, as a component of the valid RMB 10 million capital contribution, also constitutes a valid capital contribution. According to the "10.26 Agreement," the equity formed by this RMB 5 million capital contribution shall belong to Qidi Company. The 55% equity interest that Qidi Company holds in Kemei Investment Company as a shareholder, in accordance with the "10.26 Agreement" and the articles of association of Kemei Investment Company, shall be protected by law.

Qidi Company argues that disputes among shareholders concerning capital contributions, rights distribution, and other issues should be accepted by the people's court in the place of the company's domicile. However, Qidi Company did not raise any objection to jurisdiction in the original trial. Neither did Qidi Company apply for a retrial of the second-instance court's ruling on jurisdiction. Therefore, this Court will not further review Qidi Company's argument that the original trial court had improper territorial jurisdiction.

An action for confirmation of equity and an action for dissolution and liquidation of a company are independent proceedings, lacking procedural connection, and should not be consolidated for trial. Moreover, during the retrial, Guohua Company expressly stated that it waives its claims for dissolution and liquidation of Kemei Investment Company, so this Court will not adjudicate those claims.

In summary, the original trial judgment's finding that the RMB 5 million capital contribution made in the name of Qidi Company to Kemei Investment Company violated mandatory legal provisions lacks legal basis. The main grounds for Qidi Company's application for retrial are well-founded, and this Court supports them. Pursuant to Article 186 and Article 153, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders judgment as follows:

1. Reversing the Civil Judgment (2009) Yu Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 20 of the Henan High People's Court, and reversing the Civil Judgment (2007) Bian Min Chu Zi No. 69 of the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court, Henan Province;

2. Dismissing all claims of Zhengzhou Guohua Investment Co., Ltd.

Court acceptance fee for first instance: RMB 188,190.00; court acceptance fee for second instance: RMB 46,800.00. Both shall be borne by Zhengzhou Guohua Investment Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
